findings.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection')

assessment.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: CWE-93 specifically addresses CRLF sequence injection for protocol/format manipulation, not HTML attribute injection. The demonstrated vulnerability involves unquoted HTML attribute injection, not CRLF-based protocol injection.

connection.evidence: User-controlled title parameter from markdown input flows directly into unquoted HTML title attribute via string interpolation: `title=${title}`

diff_causality.evidence: If this line were reverted, the title attribute would not be rendered at all when title is null, preventing the injection vector. The addition creates the vulnerable code path.

security_control.required_control: CRLF sequence neutralization for protocol/format boundaries
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-93 requires controls specifically for CRLF sequence neutralization in protocol contexts
existing_controls_checked: No CRLF-specific validation observed in the code path
security_control.deficiency_evidence: The demonstrated issue is HTML attribute quoting deficiency, not CRLF injection. No evidence shows CRLF sequences being used as special elements or requiring neutralization.

concrete_impact.evidence: Unquoted attribute allows injection of additional HTML attributes and JavaScript via whitespace characters, enabling XSS in the Electron application context

assessment.diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the title attribute would not be rendered when title is null, eliminating the unquoted attribute injection vector entirely.
supporting_evidence: User-controlled title parameter flows directly into unquoted HTML attribute
No validation or escaping applied to title parameter before HTML construction
contradicting_evidence: CWE-93 mechanism focuses on CRLF sequence injection for protocols/formats, not HTML attribute injection
No evidence of CRLF sequences being used as special separators in this context
unresolved_facts: Whether this.options.sanitize is enabled in practice
How marked.js normalizes title parameter parsing

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: The code performs file extension validation, not authorization. CWE-863 requires an authorization check for resource access, but this is a content-type routing decision for link handling.

connection.evidence: User-controlled href from markdown content flows through extension extraction to onclick handler assignment, determining whether openMarkdownLink (internal) or openLinkWithExternalBrowser is used.

diff_causality.evidence: Adding this extension check changes link routing behavior - without it, all non-HTTP links with extensions would use cancelClick; with it, markdown extensions trigger openMarkdownLink.

security_control.required_control: Proper authorization check for file system access
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-863 requires verifying user permissions before accessing resources
existing_controls_checked: file extension validation against markdown_exts array
security_control.deficiency_evidence: The extension check is a content-type routing mechanism, not an authorization control. No user authentication or permission verification is demonstrated.

concrete_impact.evidence: Potential for file:// links with markdown extensions to bypass external browser handling, but no demonstrated authorization bypass or unauthorized access to protected resources.

assessment.diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, file:// links with extensions would not be routed to openMarkdownLink, potentially preventing internal file operations but not affecting authorization checks.
supporting_evidence: Extension validation determines link handling routing between internal and external handlers
contradicting_evidence: The mechanism is content-type routing, not authorization checking
No user authentication or permission verification is present in the demonstrated path
unresolved_facts: Implementation of element_env.openMarkdownDoc and its security controls
Source and validation of markdown_exts configuration
User authentication context for the application

findings.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command ('Command Injection')

assessment.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command ('Command Injection')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: CWE-77 specifically addresses command injection where input modifies OS/shell commands. This code performs HTML rendering and DOM manipulation, not command execution.

connection.evidence: updated_doc flows from external property binding through markdown rendering to innerHTML assignment, establishing a clear data flow path.

diff_causality.evidence: If this line were reverted, the markdown content would not be rendered to HTML and assigned to the DOM, preventing any potential injection.

security_control.required_control: Command validation/sanitization for shell/OS command injection
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-77 requires validation of input that constructs OS/shell commands
security_control.deficiency_evidence: No command execution is demonstrated; the code performs HTML rendering, not command construction

concrete_impact.evidence: No command execution mechanism is present; impact would be DOM-based (XSS) rather than command injection.

assessment.diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the markdown preview would not update with new content, preventing any rendering of potentially malicious markdown to the DOM.
supporting_evidence: External input (updated_doc) flows through rendering pipeline to innerHTML assignment
Marked library is used with custom renderer modifications
contradicting_evidence: CWE-77 requires command/OS injection context, but this code performs HTML/DOM manipulation
No shell/OS command execution is demonstrated in the code path
unresolved_facts: Whether marked is called with sanitize: true option
Source of document property values (user-controlled vs trusted)
Whether other HTML injection vectors exist beyond link protocols
